=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1663 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: §34.B's standing go ("open the issue without waiting") contradicts §31.B step 3 (lines 1486-1489) and §23.C (lines 1011-1016), which require waiting for the user's go, and neither of those carries a §34 exception.
  WHY: A session following §31.B or §23.C waits and breaks §34. A session following §34.B opens the issue and breaks §31.B step 3. No precedence rule resolves it. Reviewers rated this MAJOR.
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1663 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: §34.B ("One issue per cause", cites only §31.B step 2) omits §31.B step 4 (lines 1490-1498): one issue per repository, the `ai:engine-claude` label at creation, the `add_repo` check, and `Refs` cross-links with §19 discipline.
  WHY: A prevention issue may lack the pipeline label, span several repos, or use auto-close keywords against a tracking issue, so it never starts the pipeline or stalls the orchestrator. Reviewers rated this MAJOR.
- CLAUDE.md:1630-1631, 1659-1663 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: §34 says "not superseded by §12", but §12.A (lines 304-310, NON-NEGOTIABLE) bars follow-up PRs and requires a stop-and-ask for oversized scope, while §34.B sends larger fixes to a separate issue. The text does not say which rule wins in PR-review mode.
  WHY: In PR-review mode the outcome depends on which section the model weighs more heavily. Severity disagreement: sonnet-5_5 and glm-5_3-flash rated it NIT, while gemini and minimax rated it MAJOR.
- CLAUDE.md:1657-1658 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The §34.B small-fix bullet ("implement it in the session, with a test") has no stated precedence over the ask-first rules in §0 (lines 29-34) and §2 (lines 49-59).
  WHY: A session cannot satisfy both §0/§2 ask-first and the §34 instruction to implement. Severity disagreement: glm-5_3-flash rated it NIT, while gemini and minimax rated it MAJOR.
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1663 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The §34.B standing go has no repository-scope limit, while §34.A.2 (lines 1646-1648) sends the search to other repos. A session could open issues outside its given scope without the named ask §23.C requires (line 1006).
  WHY: A session could skip the §23.C ask for writes outside its scope. Severity disagreement: sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT. gemini and minimax rated it MAJOR. The glm-5_3-flash reviewer folded it into the §31.B step 4 finding instead of flagging it separately.
- CLAUDE.md:1678-1683 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: §34.D cites §11 ("stays open until its fix is merged, is tracked in an open issue, or the user drops it"), but §11 (lines 263-274) covers only user-provided task lists and has no such closure semantics.
  WHY: It is unclear when a prevention item counts as closed, so the citation is wording drift. All reviewers rated it NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

(No task gaps reported.)

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1663 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: Following either section breaks the other, and the text gives no precedence.
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1663 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: §34.B cites only §31.B step 2 and omits step 4's one issue per repository, the `ai:engine-claude` label, `Refs` cross-links, and the pipeline check.
  WHY: A prevention issue may lack the pipeline label, span several repos, or use auto-close keywords.
- CLAUDE.md:1630-1631 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: "not superseded by §12" does not say which rule wins against §12.A when a recurrence cause turns up during PR review.
  WHY: §12.A bars follow-up PRs, not issues, so the conflict is narrow, but the PR-review outcome is unclear without a precedence line.
- CLAUDE.md:1680-1683 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: §34.D cites §11 for "tracked in an open issue", but §11 (lines 263-274) covers only user-provided task lists.
  WHY: It is unclear when a prevention item counts as closed. This is wording drift, not a break.
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1663 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The standing go names no repository limit, and §34.A.2 sends the search to other repos, against §23.C line 1006.
  WHY: A session following §34 literally could skip the §23.C ask for writes outside its scope.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- CLAUDE.md:1661 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §34.B's standing go overrides the wait-for-go rule in §31.B step 3 and §23.C (and `.claude/docs/s23-github-access.md`).
  WHY: Following §34.B violates the mandatory ask-first rules, and following §31.B/§23.C violates §34.B.
- CLAUDE.md:1657 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The small-fix bullet ("implement it in the session, with a test") does not explicitly supersede the ask-first requirement in §0 and §2.
  WHY: It creates an instruction conflict for a session applying a small fix under §34.
- CLAUDE.md:1630-1631, 1659-1663 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §34 says "not superseded by §12", yet §12.A (NON-NEGOTIABLE) forbids follow-up PRs and mandates stop-and-ask for large fixes during PR review.
  WHY: It is ambiguous whether the standing go or the §12.A rule prevails in PR-review mode.
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1663 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §34.B mandates "One issue per cause" but not the pipeline issue conventions (`ai:engine-claude` label, `add_repo`, `Refs` cross-links, §19).
  WHY: Issues lacking the label or using auto-close keywords fail to trigger the orchestrator or stall it prematurely.
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1663 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The standing go has no repository-scope limit, while §34.A.2 references other repos.
  WHY: A session could treat it as pre-authorisation to write outside its scope, which violates §23.C.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1662 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §34.B cites §31.B step 3 as its standing go, but step 3 (lines 1486-1489) mandates waiting for the user's go before opening any issue.
  WHY: Two mandatory rules say opposite things with no precedence statement.
- CLAUDE.md:1657-1658 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The small-fix bullet conflicts with §0 (lines 29-34) and §2, which require asking before acting.
  WHY: Both cannot hold at once, and §34.B gives no precedence over §0/§2.
- CLAUDE.md:1631, 1675-1676 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §34's intro says it is not superseded by §12, and §34.C's list omits §12. §34.B's separate issue conflicts with §12.A's single-PR rule (lines 304-310).
  WHY: Both cannot be authoritative when §34 is triggered during PR review.
- CLAUDE.md:1662 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: "One issue per cause" differs from §31.B step 4's "one issue per repository" and omits the label, `add_repo` and `Refs` requirements.
  WHY: The issue may lack the pipeline label, and an auto-close keyword would fail `pr-body-lint` (§19 incident #2734).
- CLAUDE.md:1660-1661 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The standing go is not bounded to the session's repository, while §34.A.2 (lines 1646-1648) directs the search to other repos.
  WHY: A session may open issues in a consumer or other repo without the §2 ask §23.C requires.
- CLAUDE.md:1678-1683 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: §34.D borrows §11 closure semantics, but §11 covers only user task lists.
  WHY: A prevention item has no defined closed state under §11.
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1662 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The §34.B standing go pre-authorises issue creation beyond what §23.C and §31.B step 3 allowed. It is not bounded to the session's repo, and it has no kill switch or invocation guard.
  WHY: Sessions may treat it as authority across any repo the recurrence search reaches, and §23.C's named ask is not preempted, so the two clauses race for authority.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1662 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §34.B's standing go ("open the issue without waiting") contradicts §31.B step 3 (lines 1486-1489) and §23.C (lines 1011-1016). The carve-out is declared only on the §34 side, unlike the file's own convention of declaring exceptions inside §23.C.
  WHY: The outcome depends on which section the model reads first.
- CLAUDE.md:1659-1662, 1675-1676 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §34.B omits §31.B step 4's mechanics (lines 1490-1498): one issue per repository, the `ai:engine-claude` label, `add_repo`, and `Refs` cross-links. §34.C's rule list also omits §31, and "one issue per cause" collides with "one issue per repository".
  WHY: An issue without the label is invisible to the pipeline, and the omitted repo check removes the §23.C scope guard.
- CLAUDE.md:1657-1658 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The small-fix bullet extends §31.A to session-initiated fixes without precedence over §0 (lines 29-34) and §2 (lines 49-59).
  WHY: The precedence gap is real, but it is narrower than the standing-go conflict because §31.A's "clear cause and fix" condition limits when it applies.
- CLAUDE.md:1630-1631 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: "not superseded by §12" does not say which rule wins against §12.A and §12.B when a recurrence cause turns up under §12.
  WHY: In PR-review mode the outcome depends on which mandatory section the model weighs more heavily.
- CLAUDE.md:1682-1683 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: §34.D cites §11 (lines 263-274), which has no "stays open until fix is merged / tracked in open issue" closure semantics.
  WHY: The reporting requirement is anchored to a rule that does not define it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
